doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Pay for charts and on the road with Ozzie
summary: He got $35 a chart and copied them himself; on the road he made $110 a week and sent $80 home.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did Ozzie have you on a salary?
Or were you paid by the piece?
No it was just kind of a stock thing. I mean back in those days I think I got $35 a chart, and I copied it too.
But thirty-five bucks then would be like thirty-five hundred now.
So you felt like man this is, I’m doing great here.

Well I went on the road with him I think for eight weeks. I made $110 a week and I sent 80 home every week. I lived on 30 bucks, like a king. Anything I wanted to eat, anywhere I wanted to eat, hotels, the whole thing, 30 dollars. This is 1942. And then I got
